title: York Furnace Code 1 Blink: Flame detected when the gas valve should be off
meaning: The control sensed flame without a call for heat.
commonCauses: A gas valve leaking or stuck open
A shorted flame-sensing circuit
A failed integrated control board
whenToCallPro: Turn the furnace off and call a licensed technician immediately to test the gas valve and flame-proving circuit.
dangerNote: Turn the furnace off and do not reset it. If you smell gas, leave the building without operating switches and contact the gas utility or emergency services from outside.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 1 Blink means the control sensed flame without a call for heat on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 2 Blinks: Pressure switch was closed at the wrong time
meaning: The pressure switch was stuck closed when it should have been open.
commonCauses: A pressure switch stuck closed
A pinched or incorrectly connected pressure hose
Shorted pressure-switch wiring or a control fault
diySteps: Turn furnace power off for five minutes and do not bypass or jumper the pressure switch.
Check only the outdoor vent openings for obvious snow, ice, leaves, or nests before restoring power once.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the code returns; the switch, hose, wiring, and inducer draft need testing.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 2 Blinks means the pressure switch was stuck closed when it should have been open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 3 Blinks: Pressure-switch circuit did not close
meaning: The pressure switch failed to close after the inducer started.
commonCauses: A blocked intake or exhaust vent
A restricted condensate drain or pressure hose
A weak inducer motor or pressure switch
diySteps: With the furnace off, check outdoor intake and exhaust openings for snow, ice, leaves, or nests.
Replace a visibly dirty air filter, restore power once, and note whether the code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the vent is clear and the pressure-switch code returns; combustion-air testing requires instruments.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 3 Blinks means the pressure switch failed to close after the inducer started on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 4 Blinks: Limit circuit opened
meaning: The primary or auxiliary limit circuit is open.
commonCauses: A dirty or overly restrictive air filter
Closed or blocked supply and return vents
A blower, limit switch, or airflow problem
diySteps: Turn the furnace off and replace a dirty filter with the size and type specified for the system.
Open all supply registers and make sure return grilles are not blocked before trying one reset.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the limit code returns; repeated overheating can damage the furnace.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 4 Blinks means the primary or auxiliary limit circuit is open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 5 Blinks: Flame-rollout safety lockout
commonCauses: A blocked flue or combustion-air path
A burner or gas-pressure problem
A damaged or restricted heat exchanger
whenToCallPro: Leave the furnace off and call a licensed technician for a combustion-safety inspection.
dangerNote: Keep the furnace off. Do not reset a rollout switch. If you smell gas or a carbon-monoxide alarm sounds, leave the building and contact emergency services or the gas utility.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 5 Blinks means the flame-rollout switch is open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 6 Blinks: Pressure-switch cycle lockout
meaning: The pressure switch opened four times during one heat call, causing lockout.
commonCauses: A blocked intake or exhaust vent
A restricted condensate drain or pressure hose
A weak inducer motor or pressure switch
diySteps: With the furnace off, check outdoor intake and exhaust openings for snow, ice, leaves, or nests.
Replace a visibly dirty air filter, restore power once, and note whether the code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the vent is clear and the pressure-switch code returns; combustion-air testing requires instruments.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 6 Blinks means the pressure switch opened four times during one heat call, causing lockout on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.

title: York Furnace Code 7 Blinks: Ignition or flame-proving failure
meaning: The burners failed to establish flame and the furnace entered ignition lockout.
commonCauses: No gas reaching the burners
A failed hot-surface igniter
A dirty or weak flame sensor
diySteps: Confirm the thermostat is calling for heat and the gas shutoff has not been moved.
Turn furnace power off for five minutes, restore it once, and note whether the same code returns.
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed technician if ignition fails again after one reset or if you smell gas.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 7 Blinks means the burners failed to establish flame and the furnace entered ignition lockout on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 8 Blinks: Flame-loss recycle lockout
meaning: Flame was lost five times during one heat call, causing recycle lockout.
commonCauses: A dirty or weak flame sensor
Unstable gas pressure or burner flame
Poor grounding or flame-sensor wiring
diySteps: Confirm the gas shutoff has not been moved and the furnace panel is fully seated.
Try one reset and watch whether the burners light and then shut off again.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if flame drops out again or ignition becomes delayed or noisy.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 8 Blinks means flame was lost five times during one heat call, causing recycle lockout on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 9 Blinks: Power polarity or grounding fault
meaning: The furnace detected reversed line polarity or an improper ground.
commonCauses: Reversed line and neutral wiring
A missing or poor equipment ground
Incorrect transformer phasing on twinned furnaces
diySteps: Turn the furnace off at its service switch.
Do not alter line-voltage wiring or grounding connections yourself.
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed technician or electrician to verify polarity, grounding, and supply voltage.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 9 Blinks means the furnace detected reversed line polarity or an improper ground on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.
modelScope: Johnson Controls integrated furnace controls using the documented 1–12 red-flash table.

title: York Furnace Code 12 Blinks: Igniter circuit fault
commonCauses: A cracked or open hot-surface igniter
Loose or damaged igniter wiring
A failed igniter relay on the control board
diySteps: Turn power off and look through the burner-viewing area for an obviously cracked igniter without touching it.
Restore power once and observe whether the igniter glows; do not continue resetting the furnace.
whenToCallPro: Call a technician if the igniter does not glow or the fault returns.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 12 Blinks means the igniter circuit is open on the supported control family. Confirm the model number and diagnostic chart inside the furnace door before replacing parts.

title: York Furnace Code 13 Blinks: External Lockout
meaning: Thirteen blinks mean an external safety opened the circuit.
commonCauses: Tripped limit
Open rollout
Loose harness
diySteps: Turn off power.
Check access panels.
Allow cooldown before reset.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 13 Blinks means Thirteen blinks mean an external safety opened the circuit. Most often from tripped limit. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $150–$600.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: York Furnace Code 14 Blinks: Thermostat Fault
meaning: Fourteen blinks indicate a thermostat signal problem.
commonCauses: Stat off or in cool
Loose wire
Dead batteries
diySteps: Set stat to heat.
Replace batteries.
Check furnace door.
whenToCallPro: Wiring service if stat is calling but code remains.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 14 Blinks means Fourteen blinks indicate a thermostat signal problem. Often caused by stat off or in cool. Usually safe to try basic checks yourself; professional repairs run $100–$350.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.

title: York Furnace Code 15 Blinks: Ignitor Circuit Fault
meaning: Fifteen blinks mean the ignitor circuit failed a check.
commonCauses: Cracked ignitor
Open wire
Board fault
diySteps: Turn off power.
Inspect ignitor.
Reseat connector.
whenToCallPro: Replace ignitor or call for board service.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 15 Blinks means Fifteen blinks mean the ignitor circuit failed a check. Most often from cracked ignitor. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $150–$450.

title: York Furnace Code 16 Blinks: Flame Lost During Run
meaning: Sixteen blinks indicate flame was lost while heating.
commonCauses: Dirty sensor
Draft
Cracked exchanger
diySteps: Clean sensor.
Check for soot.
Reset once.
whenToCallPro: Flame loss during run needs professional inspection.
snippetAnswer: York furnace code 16 Blinks means Sixteen blinks indicate flame was lost while heating. Most often from dirty sensor. You can check basics first; professional repairs typically run $100–$3500.
modelScope: No universal meaning is confirmed for this code. The exact model number and control-board chart are required.
